title: Vegan Tuna from Watermelon: Marinaded Watermelon Planks Baked as a Tuna Substitute
summary: In this Goodful episode from the Vegan Substitute series, Merle invites Mae to tackle a viral idea: turning a watermelon into a tuna substitute. They name the watermelon “Victor,” trim and skin it, and cut four planks to marinate. The marinade combines rice wine vinegar, low-sodium soy sauce (or tamari), sesame oil, neutral oil, red pepper flakes, and crumbled nori to impart a fishy flavor. The planks are vacuum-sealed and refrigerated for six hours or overnight, then dried and baked on parchment at a low oven (300°F / 150°C) for 90 minutes. After cooling, the slices are plated on sushi rice and taste-tested by Merle and Mae. The hosts discuss texture, flavor, and the substitution’s viability, noting that while it resembles tuna in appearance and mouthfeel, the flavor remains distinctly watermelon. The video frames the experiment as a playful, competitive cooking challenge within the series, and touches on sustainability practices like composting towels and reusing bags.
topics: Marinade ingredients (rice wine vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, neutral oil)

sections.title: Watermelon prep and planking
sections.description: Merle prepares the watermelon, trims the rind and white pith, and begins cutting the fruit into four planks named 'Victor' to become the tuna-substitute base.

sections.title: Marinade preparation
sections.description: The hosts assemble the marinade with rice wine vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, neutral oil, red pepper flakes, and crumbled nori to simulate a fishy profile for the watermelon.

sections.title: Marinating and refrigeration
sections.description: Watermelon planks are vacuum-sealed with the marinade and chilled for six hours or overnight, with emphasis on removing air from the bags.

sections.title: Baking and finishing
sections.description: Planks are removed from bags, dried, placed on parchment, and baked at 300°F (150°C) for 90 minutes, then allowed to cool before slicing.

sections.title: Taste test and evaluation
sections.description: The finished product is sliced into 1-inch diagonals, plated on sushi rice, and tasted by Merle and Mae. They discuss texture and flavor, concluding the dish resembles watermelon more than traditional tuna, and assign qualitative ratings for likeness and overall dish quality.

Marinade composition to mimic seafood flavor (rice wine vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, neutral oil, red pepper flakes, crumbled nori)
Low-oven baking of marinated watermelon planks (300°F / 150°C for 90 minutes) to achieve texture
